html:
The Chora church is a Byzantine church in the northwest of Constantinople, near the land walls, famous for mosaics and frescoes made between about 1315 and 1321. It is now the Kariye Mosque in Istanbul.

It belonged to an old monastery. The statesman and scholar Theodore Metochites, chief minister of Emperor Andronikos II, paid to rebuild and decorate it. A mosaic over a door shows him kneeling to offer the church to Christ, wearing his huge hat.

The mosaics tell the lives of the Virgin and of Christ in lively, crowded scenes. In the side chapel built for burials, a fresco of the Anastasis shows Christ pulling Adam and Eve from their tombs, one of the best known images of Byzantine art. Together they are the finest surviving work of the late Byzantine revival under the Palaiologos dynasty.

When Andronikos fell in 1328, Metochites lost everything and later retired to the Chora as a monk. The Ottomans made the church a mosque in the early 16th century. It was a museum from 1945 and became a mosque again in 2020.
sum: The Chora church is a Byzantine church in the northwest of Constantinople, near the land walls, famous for mosaics and frescoes made between about 1315 and 1321. It is now the Kariye Mosque in Istanbul.
